rules.statement: Select an elliptic curve by its identity (curve name or named-curve OID), never by key size alone, and use a size lookup only when no other registered curve shares that size.
rules.why: A size doesn't identify a curve: secp256k1 and P-256 are both 256-bit. A size-keyed lookup can't generate a chosen same-size curve and gives the wrong curve name for a non-NIST key.
rules.check: Look for curve lookups, switches or dictionaries keyed by bit size (256/384/521) that map to a curve or a `crv` value, when same-size curves can exist.

rules.statement: When publishing an EC key as a JWK, take the `crv` value from the key's actual named-curve OID, not from its key size.
rules.why: Deriving `crv` from size gives the wrong name for keys on non-NIST curves that share a size with a NIST curve.
rules.check: Look at JWK export code that sets `crv` from `KeySize` or a size-based mapping instead of from `ECParameters.Curve.Oid`.

rules.statement: Keep elliptic-curve knowledge in one extensible catalog that generation, validation and JWK publication all read, and don't add a separate curve registry or hard-coded curve list for any one of them.
rules.why: Separate registries for generation and publication drift apart, and a curve set fixed in code can't be extended.
rules.check: Look for new curve tables, switches or registries in generation, JWKS or UI code that duplicate the shared curve catalog.

rules.statement: Before handing an imported elliptic-curve public point (a JWK `x`/`y`, or an ECDH-ES peer key) to the platform, check that each coordinate is exactly the field's byte length (RFC 7518 §6.2.1.2–3), is below the prime p, and satisfies the curve equation, and throw `ArgumentException` if any check fails.
rules.why: An off-curve peer point is an invalid-curve attack on key agreement. The platform also rejects such points with different exception types on different operating systems (CNG throws `PlatformNotSupportedException`, OpenSSL throws `CryptographicException`).
rules.check: Look for EC public key import paths (`ECDiffieHellman`/`ECDsa.ImportParameters` from JWK or peer input) that skip a coordinate-length, range and on-curve check before import.

rules.statement: Check an elliptic-curve point with the curve's domain constants (p, a, b), not with domain parameters read from the platform at run time such as `ExportExplicitParameters`.
rules.why: The platform doesn't offer explicit parameters for every curve on every operating system, so the check would depend on the platform again. Constants make it the same everywhere.
rules.check: Look for point validation that calls `ExportExplicitParameters` or otherwise asks the platform for the curve domain during validation.

rules.statement: Don't catch `PlatformNotSupportedException` alongside `CryptographicException` to report it as an invalid key. Let the platform's own failures, such as an unsupported curve, surface with their original exception.
rules.why: Catching it hides a real unsupported-curve error as an invalid point and leaves validity defined by the platform.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks or exception filters around key import that merge `PlatformNotSupportedException` into an invalid-key or `CryptographicException` path.

rules.statement: A key generator rejects parameters that don't apply to its key type: it rejects a requested size that differs from the named curve's size, and symmetric and RSA generators reject a curve argument instead of ignoring it.
rules.why: Generation takes the curve by identity, so a mismatched size or a meaningless curve signals a wrong request and must not be silently dropped.
rules.check: Look for key-generation code that ignores a supplied curve for RSA or symmetric keys, or accepts a key size that conflicts with the requested curve.

rules.statement: A registered elliptic-curve specification must supply its short-Weierstrass domain (p, a, b), from constants or read from a platform-supported curve, so that its points can be validated.
rules.why: Without the domain, points on that curve can't be checked independently of the platform before import.
rules.check: Look for new curve specifications or registrations that leave the domain out or set it to null.
